findings.title: Plaintext passwords and PII are written to logs
findings.explanation: The PR description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields. It doesn't. `src/lib/logger.ts` redacts only `authorization` and `token` (`REDACTED_KEYS`). `req.body` on signup contains `password`, which this line logs in cleartext, along with `email` and `organization`. Logs usually have wider access and longer retention than the database, and passwords are stored there only as hashes. Logging them is a credential leak and a likely compliance problem (GDPR, SOC2). It also breaks `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` line 23: 'Never log request bodies or headers on auth routes.' Remove this line. If you need to debug failed signups, log only non-sensitive metadata. Examples are the key names present (`Object.keys(req.body)`), the zod issue paths and codes from a `safeParse` failure, and field types or lengths. Never log values. Also log the validation failure rather than the raw input.

findings.title: Validation failures are not captured, which is the actual debugging goal
findings.explanation: `signupSchema.parse` throws a ZodError, and the global handler in `server.ts` logs only `err.message`. Use `safeParse` on failure and log `error.issues` with only the `path` and `code` of each issue, not the input values. Then return a 400 with those issues. This answers 'why did the signup fail' without logging the payload. Pre-validation logging also records attempts that would never succeed, so it adds noise.

findings.title: Redaction list is too narrow to rely on
findings.explanation: The logger redacts only `authorization` and `token`. Anyone who assumes it is safe, as this PR did, can leak secrets. Consider adding `password`, `password_hash`, `secret`, `cookie`, `api_key` and similar to the default list. Better still, use an allowlist for auth routes. This does not replace removing the log line.

findings.title: Rotate or purge logs if this was deployed
findings.explanation: If this change has reached any environment, the logs already hold plaintext passwords. Purge or scrub those logs, and consider forcing resets for the affected users.
